newsitem.title: USA: Dole says foreign funds lead to White House.
newsitem.headline: Dole says foreign funds lead to White House.

text.p: Republican presidential challenger Bob Dole fired more ammunition at President Bill Clinton on Friday, alleging that improper foreign campaign funds to Democrats lead right to his White House office.
The underdog, also trying to light a spark in his own campaign, remains far behind in polls but aides said he is catching up as time runs short to the Nov. 5 election.

Dole and aides honed in on the campaign financing issue here and in Albuquerque earlier when he told the New Mexico rally he wanted to restore values to the White House instead of "slippery liberalism."

"Follow the money," Dole intoned in Albuquerque, claiming the foreign contributions would lead to the White House although he gave no evidence to substantiate the innuendo that Clinton was involved or did anything wrong.

In recent days, Dole's new get-tough tactics have hit hard at alleged "scandals" and ethical lapses he sees at the White House -- underscoring reports about questionable contributions from people associated with Indonesian, South Korean and other foreign interests into the Democratic Party.
At a school rally here, he hammered away at the foreign contribution issue before several thousand cheering students at a middle school who seemed to be unaware of what he was talking about.
Dole said federal laws should be changed to bar foreigners from making contributions. Non-citizens now are generally barred from giving political money but there are exceptions.

He charged that Democrats are running negative ads against him and "a lot of those ads that are being run are probably being paid for with some of this foreign money. I say it is time to say if you are not a citizen you can't contribute to a political campaign in the United States of America and it is time we changed the law."
"This abuse of the political process must stop and if I'm president of the United States it is going to stop," Dole said.

In New Mexico earlier, Dole said, "Every day we have a new scandal involving the foreign corruption of America. Our elections are not for sale to some foreign influence or some foreign interest. This is the United States of America."

"Make no mistake about it, a public office is a public trust. And it's time to restore that trust in America and it's time to return values to America in exchange for slippery liberalism in the Clinton administration and bring back common sense and integrity to the White House," he said.

His attack, which drew strong applause, intensified the assault on what Republicans charge is ethical misconduct in the White House. He urged Clinton to "give an accounting" of foreign contributions and said that if the money is tracked, "it rolls all the way down to the (White House) Oval Office."
"We're going to get tough with this guy," said Dole, who sounded hoarse after a string of rallies and speeches in California before coming to New Mexico.
New Mexico's Republican Sen. Pete Domenici lauded Dole's effort to attack Clinton on ethics and said Dole should have gone on the offensive earlier.
"He should have made the whole campaign on sleaze," Domenici told Reuters.
